title: Pelorus Finance LLM migration discovery
header: Date: 2026-04-25 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC; Duration: 54 minutes; Location: Zoom; Recording: enabled; Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Pelorus Head of ML), Diego Alvarez (Pelorus Platform), Rina Shah (Pelorus Security), Tom Bennett (Pelorus Product)
summary: Discovery to understand Pelorus's requirement to exit current hosted provider for inference, evaluate parity with current vLLM/TGI-based stack, and surface security and deployment constraints for hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Agreement to run an eval benchmark and exchange security artifacts.
topics: security: KMS, SOC2, VPC, audit logs
next_steps: Samir to send SOC2 and security whitepaper + KMS integration notes (by 2026-04-28)
Maya to share benchmark template and example vLLM config (by 2026-04-27)
Pelorus to provide sample prompt set and production traffic profile (by 2026-05-04)
action_items: Samir Patel: Email SOC2 and KMS doc (2026-04-28)
Maya Chen: Share benchmark sheet and example TGI config (2026-04-27)
Laura Kim: Upload 2 representative prompt sets and traffic histogram to shared drive (2026-05-04)
Diego Alvarez: Confirm network constraints for private deployment (2026-05-01)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Samir Patel from Redwood here, Maya Chen our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Maya: Hi!
[00:10] Laura: Hi Samir, Laura here.
[00:12] Diego: Diego on the line.
[00:14] Rina: Rina, security.
[00:16] Tom: Tom from Product.
[00:18] Samir: Awesome, thanks. The goal for today is to understand your current inference stack, what you need to keep parity on, and the constraints that drive hosted vs dedicated vs private. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:30] Laura: Great — quick context: Pelorus is a fintech risk platform. We run multiple real-time scoring models and conversational ops for merchant support. Currently we're on "Orion AI" hosted endpoints for generation and we host smaller models ourselves using vLLM and TGI for batched jobs. The thing is latency spikes and cost have been trending up, also their recent token pricing change pushed us to look at alternatives.
[00:52] Samir: Totally, that's familiar. When you say latency spikes, is that tail latency on single-turn requests or on the long-context sessions?
[00:58] Laura: Mostly single-turn scoring — we have an embedding + rerank + generation pipeline. The reranker calls are strict under 120ms median, but tail goes to 700 to 800ms sometimes. And also cold K/V cache issues — hmm kv cache, sorry — cold KV cache misses with our vLLM offload.
[01:20] Diego: To add, we batch a lot overnight with TGI-based jobs for model finetune and audit, but production is mostly near real-time. We currently use a mix: hosted for large open models and self-hosted vLLM for mid-sized quantized ones.
[01:33] Maya: Got it. Two parallel workloads then — production latency-sensitive, and batch/finetune throughput. For migration we typically look at whether you want full managed (hosted), reserved capacity (Dedicated), or private deployment inside your VPC. Any preference?
[01:46] Tom: Short-term we want a quick hosted path to stop paying the token premium, but long-term we'd like private for compliance if that becomes mandatory.
[01:55] Rina: Compliance is the driver for us — SOC 2 is table stakes, but we also have contractual data residency and KMS/HSM requirements for certain customers. So private deployment or VPC-backed private plane is attractive.
[02:08] Samir: Makes sense. On the KMS front, Redwood integrates with customer KMS and HSM — we've done both AWS KMS CMKs and customer-managed HSMs for encryption at rest and key wrapping. We can include audit log retention options.
[02:21] Rina: How mature is that integration? I need to know if our key rotation and split-knowledge policies can be preserved.
[02:27] Maya: We've onboarded enterprise customers with rotate policies; it's a config mapping. I'll follow up with the integration notes.
[02:33] Diego: A question on compatibility — our stack relies on vLLM state management and a particular TGI server config for kv cache and sharded attention kernels. How much work is it to port those models over?
[02:46] Maya: Good question. For the majority of open models we've seen, the model files load fine; the primary differences are in runtimes — Redwood's serving runtime supports kernels and quantization paths that map to your weights, but there are cases where tensor layout or custom TGI plugins need adaptation. We do a short compatibility pass where we check model file, tokenizer mismatch, and a light inference run. That will tell us if there's any conversion required.
[03:12] Laura: Are there runtime-equivalence guarantees? We need eval parity — if we move, we can't have a regression in accuracy or prompt behavior.
[03:20] Samir: We don't promise bit-for-bit equivalence because core ops can differ, but we do benchmark on your prompt set and compare output distributions, perplexity, and a small human eval for critical prompts. We can also pin model versions and roll back.
[03:36] Tom: How do you measure parity? We have golden prompts plus scoring heuristics.
[03:41] Maya: We take your golden set, run on both sides with matched seeds/temps, and compute overlap metrics, regression delta on scoring, and human spot checks. We capture diffs in a report.
[03:51] Diego: What about latency and batching — we use continuous batching in vLLM to maximize GPU utilization. Does Redwood support similar batching without inflating tail latency?
[04:01] Maya: Yes, our runtime supports continuous batching and adaptive batching policies. You can set strict SLOs so the runtime prioritizes latency over throughput, or vice versa. There's also prefix caching and KV cache reuse for ongoing conversations to reduce work.
[04:15] Laura: On KV cache reuse — our current pattern keeps per-session KV cache for 30 minutes; we need equivalent TTL and eviction semantics. Is that configurable?
[04:24] Maya: Totally configurable. TTLs, eviction policies, and cache sizing can be tuned; we also provide metrics per model to find hot prefixes.
[04:31] Rina: From a security perspective, we need RBAC, SSO (SAML/Okta), audit trails, and storage encryption. Also question: will logs ever contain PII? If so, can we mask or redact at ingest?
[04:44] Samir: We offer RBAC and SSO integrations; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. For logs containing PII, we support configurable redaction at the gateway and also token-level scrubbers — we can default to redaction on Private deployments.
[04:57] Tom: Pricing — you said dedicated reserved capacity is for throughput. What's the rough delta between hosted per-token and dedicated committed?
[05:04] Samir: Ballpark, dedicated reserved can be 30-60% cheaper on unit cost depending on commit and model family because you pay for capacity not per token. We'll run your profile through our pricing model and show a forecast.
[05:16] Diego: We'll need an apples-to-apples comparison with our current provider. They have some hidden cold-start costs for large context runs.
[05:23] Maya: We'll include cold-start/caching assumptions in the benchmark template.
[05:28] Laura: Ok, technical specifics — our largest model is a quantized 13B with custom kernels. We use TGI with some patches for fused attention. Can Redwood run patched TGI plugins or do we need to change those?
[05:41] Maya: We prefer to upstream runtime-level tuning into our kernel set; we can either adopt your patches upstream or run a private build in Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted, plugins are limited for security/stability, so some patches might need refactor. But many times the ops can be mapped to existing fused kernels. We'll do a compatibility report.
[05:58] Diego: Network and data residency: if we do private deployment, we need it in Azure West Europe region; also egress policies prevent external model downloads. Does Redwood support air-gapped model injection?
[06:12] Samir: Yes — private deployment supports air-gapped model import and an offline bundle process. For Azure West Europe, we've deployed in customer VPCs before. We'll document the pull/push process for images and model artifacts.
[06:23] Rina: And audit: retention windows, immutable logs for 7 years?
[06:27] Maya: We can configure retention; long-term immutable archives are available via S3-compatible cold storage. We'll include options in the security doc.
[06:36] Tom: Operationally, who owns the rollout? Our Platform will own integration points, but Product owns acceptance. Does Redwood support canary and A/B rollouts?
[06:45] Samir: Yes — rollouts, canaries, automatic fallback policies, and route-based traffic splitting are part of Redwood Console. You can do canary percentages and auto-fallback to a pinned variant if quality or latency thresholds break.
[06:58] Laura: We care about retraining/finetune pipeline compat — we re-finetune lightweight adapters and serve them. Is there a way to attach a finetuned weights layer to the model in Redwood without re-serving a whole image?
[07:10] Maya: We support adapter-style weights for many model families; you can upload delta weights and the runtime composes them at load. For some formats we may need a conversion step.
[07:20] Diego: One of our biggest fears is silent behavior drift after migration. How do you support monitoring and regression detection in prod?
[07:27] Samir: Redwood Optimize ties model performance to prompt sets and provides regression alerts. You can set quality thresholds on your golden prompts and trigger rollbacks or alerts. Also token-level cost and latency breakdowns are available.
[07:40] Rina: For legal: will logs be available for eDiscovery?
[07:43] Samir: Yes, audit/export features are there; on Private deployment you retain full control. For Hosted we provide configurable retention and export hooks.
[07:50] Tom: Can we do a short POC — baseline parity and latency check on our 13B quant model and reranker?
[07:56] Maya: Absolutely. Typical POC: 2-week benchmark run — we onboard model, run parity checks on golden set, measure latency under load, and provide a cost forecast. We usually recommend Dedicated for parity-focused tests if you want exact infra match. For speed, Hosted with pinned instance types works too.
[08:12] Diego: We need to reproduce our vLLM batching behavior to see tail latency. Will Redwood let us configure batching policy and queueing behavior?
[08:19] Maya: Yes, batching policy is configurable, including max batch size, wait window, and priority queues.
[08:24] Laura: About model conversion — do you have a converter for TGI artifacts?
[08:29] Maya: We have conversion scripts for common forks and formats; if it's custom, we'll do a one-time conversion and keep that in your artifact repo.
[08:36] Rina: Quick question on SSO: we use Okta and SCIM. Any gotchas?
[08:40] Samir: Okta and SCIM are supported for provisioning; we can enable SAML-based SSO. We'll share our SSO integration guide.
[08:49] Tom: On SLA — what's Redwood's uptime SLA for Dedicated?
[08:52] Samir: Dedicated comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency targets in the contract. Hosted has best-effort SLOs with tiered support.
[09:02] Laura: One more — data retention for prompts: we have contractual constraints to purge certain customer PII after 30 days. Can Redwood enforce that?
[09:11] Maya: Yes. Retention and deletion policies can be enforced and audited; we'll include deletion runbooks.
[09:18] Diego: Ok, what's the onboarding timeline if we start POC next week?
[09:22] Samir: For a Hosted POC, we can spin up pinned hosts and get you running in 3-5 business days once we have model artifacts and creds. Dedicated or Private will take longer — Dedicated maybe 2-3 weeks for capacity and sizing, Private (VPC/on-prem) could be 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals.
[09:38] Tom: Are there any known regressions moving from vLLM/TGI to Redwood runtime for quantized models?
[09:44] Maya: Not generically, but custom fused ops occasionally change numerical behavior. That's why we do the parity eval and human spot-check.
[09:50] Laura: Ok let's recap and next steps.
[09:53] Samir: Recap: Redwood to share security artifacts (SOC2, KMS notes), Maya to share benchmark template and conversion guidance, Pelorus to provide prompt set + traffic profile, then schedule a 2-week POC focusing on 13B quant model and reranker. We'll include pricing/forecast.
[10:11] Rina: Sounds good. I want to review KMS rotation details before the POC.
[10:15] Samir: We'll send detailed KMS rotation and HSM notes.
[10:18] Diego: I'll start prepping the prompt sets and a traffic histogram.
[10:21] Tom: I'll align Product acceptance criteria and golden prompts.
[10:25] Samir: Great. Any final questions?
[10:27] Laura: No, that's it. Thank you.
[10:29] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed schedule. Link to share: deck and benchmark template will be uploaded to the drive.
[10:37] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and partial inaudible segments. There were a couple of fast interjections around the model plugin discussion that didn't fully transcribe.
